sources.note: Nothing. Sections: 2 Syllable (p.5-6), 3 Sound inventory incl. 3.3.1 vowel lengthening (p.7-16), 4 Tone (p.17-18: lexical + grammatical tone, H, L, rising, falling, possible M), 5 remarks on Schaub/Akeriweh. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + read).

sources.citation: Lonbeck, Janelle. 2013. The Noun Phrase in Kenswei Nsei (Bamessing). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 54 pp. (Glottolog ref 550423)
sources.note: Nothing. Morphosyntax of the NP; transcription conventions (p.10-11) mark surface tone H/L/M(downstepped H) on every syllable; sec. 1.3 surveys previous work (Schaub 1978, Akeriweh 2000, DeVries 2008a/b). No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: DeVries, Aaron. 2008b. Kenswey Nsey (Bamessing): Orthography Guide. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 18 pp. (SIL archives item 52081)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Tone (p.12-13): four surface tones (H, L, rising, falling); only H marked, contour tones written with doubled vowels 'because length has not been found to be a contrastive element'. No stress/accent statement.
